name: Engineering Services Officer
title: Indian Engineering Services (UPSC ESE)
intro: From Class 12 PCM to a Group A engineering officer: a B.E./B.Tech in Civil, Mechanical, Electrical or E&T, the three-stage UPSC ESE (prelims, mains, personality test), then department training and posting.

phases.title: Class 12 PCM and engineering entrance
phases.summary: PCM leads to the B.E./B.Tech that ESE requires.
points: Class 12 PCM is the route to engineering entrance exams.
Commerce and Arts are not eligible routes.
Pick a branch that ESE covers: Civil, Mechanical, Electrical, or Electronics & Telecommunication.

phases.title: B.E. / B.Tech
phases.summary: A degree in engineering from a recognised university.
points: You need a degree in engineering, or an equivalent the notice accepts (some posts accept specific M.Sc degrees).
Final-year students can usually apply if they produce the degree by the date in the notice.
Age limits and relaxations are in the current UPSC notice.

phases.title: ESE Prelims
phases.summary: Objective papers: general studies & engineering aptitude, plus your discipline.
points: Paper on general studies and engineering aptitude.
ESE is not GATE — GATE is for postgraduate admission and some PSU hiring.

phases.title: ESE Mains and personality test
phases.summary: Two conventional discipline papers, then the UPSC interview.
points: Mains: conventional (descriptive) papers in your discipline.
Those who qualify in the Mains face a personality test by UPSC.
Medical and physical standards apply for the services you choose.

phases.title: Training, posting and growth
phases.summary: Department training, then field posting as a Group A officer.
points: Entry: Group A central services start at Level 10 of the 7th CPC pay matrix (₹56,100 entry basic), plus DA, HRA and other allowances.
Growth path: Assistant Executive Engineer → Executive Engineer → Superintending → Chief Engineer.
Related routes: GATE-based PSU recruitment and state engineering services.
